articles.title: Japanese Prime Minister Takaichi rejects criticism around weak yen and high interest rates
articles.summary: Takaichi also said that her administration will increase confidence in the yen by building a strong economy. Japan's exports have been partly boosted by yen's depreciation, as a weak currency makes exports more competitive. For bond markets, Takaichi said that "We intend to appropriately control the amount of government bond issuance," at a time when yields have been rising as Japan's central bank raises its policy rate and continues to normalize its monetary policy.

articles.title: China's third-quarter economic growth quickens to 4.5% as exports surge, beating estimates
articles.summary: China's economic growth accelerated to 4.5% in the third quarter from a year earlier, as robust foreign demand for the country's technological goods largely offset drags from a deepening property slump and sluggish consumer demand. The data shows an economy still leaning on factories and overseas buyers while households and private investors hold back, with growth through the first nine months averaging 4.6%, broadly in line with Beijing's official target range of 4.5% to 5%.

articles.title: Indonesian stocks plunge to six-year low as MSCI downgrade fears mount
articles.summary: Indonesia's benchmark stock index plunged over 5% on Monday to its lowest level in six years, as concerns over a potential downgrade by MSCI intensified fears of further foreign investor outflows. The MSCI Indonesia Index has fallen 47% this year as of Friday, data provided by the bank showed, with foreign investors withdrawing a net $5.1 billion from Indonesian equities over the period.

articles.title: China's CXMT sees shares drop over 6% as investors look past chipmaker's profit turnaround
articles.summary: Shares of ChangXin Memory Technologies, or CXMT, fell 6.5% Monday even as the company on Friday forecast a sharp swing to profitability for the first nine months of 2026. The company attributed the sharp improvement to rapidly growing demand for AI computing power since the second half of 2025, which has boosted the global DRAM market, leading to supply shortages and significant price increases, according to the filing.

articles.title: Anthropic commits 5% of shares to new public benefit fund that could address AI job disruption
articles.summary: Anthropic said Sunday it plans to commit 5% of its shares to a new public benefit fund, with the stake potentially increasing as the company's valuation grows. Subject to shareholder approval, the fund would immediately commit 5% of Anthropic's shares, with the board adding, at its discretion, an additional 2% for every 50% increase in the company's value above a set baseline that has yet to be disclosed.

articles.title: Brent crude hovers near $109 a barrel as Ukraine resumes energy strikes, tankers attacked in Middle East
articles.summary: Crude oil prices hovered near recent highs on Sunday as traders weighed a Ukraine bombing of oil facilities in Russia and more tankers coming under attack in the Persian Gulf. Petersburg exports about 120,000 barrels per day of refined products, mostly fuel oil, according to data from Kpler. Iran has escalated attacks on tankers in the Persian Gulf, Strait of Hormuz and Gulf of Oman in an effort to choke off crude oil exports from the region.

articles.title: India’s Finance Minister blames easy exits and excess liquidity for equity market's underperformance
articles.summary: Since January, India's key benchmark indexes have slipped nearly 12%, as per LSEG data, even though the country's economic growth has been resilient amid trade uncertainty and geopolitical shocks. India has gained a reputation as an anti-artificial intelligence trade, while markets like Taiwan and Korea, with AI champions, have attracted strong investment flows.
